tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (agent won't start, gateway fails, returns nothing, behaves differently in prod, which version is live) rather than internal implementation, and explicitly lists trigger contexts even when the user doesn't name AgentCore/Agents Classic directly ('even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name'). It is a single, dense but still bounded paragraph.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when an agent will not start or cannot be invoked, when a gateway or action group fails, when an agent returns nothing or produces no traces, when it behaves differently in production than in test, or when someone asks which agent version is actually live, even if they do not mention runtime roles, VPC endpoints, service control policies, OTLP telemetry or aliasing by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body is dense but almost entirely domain-specific: AWS API names, check-ids, specific traps, and migration guidance that an agent would not already know. There is no explanation of generic concepts like what an AWS account or IAM is.
tests.evidence: "Simulate the runtime role with iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy for every action it exercises (bedrock:InvokeModel*, s3:GetObject for sources...)" — this is specific, non-generic domain content throughout.

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body's tables and procedures are concise pointers into references/ catalogs rather than embedding full check tables, thresholds, or API docs inline. Even the comparison table and router table are summaries, not full reference dumps.
tests.evidence: "Every finding is grounded in the catalogs under references/: checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001..010...) and checks-agents.md (LLM-AGT-001..011...)" — detail is deferred to references, not embedded.

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: All five reference files are linked via markdown links in the body (Router table and Appendix).
tests.evidence: "references/checks-agentcore.md" linked as `references/checks-agentcore.md` (LLM-AC-001) and similarly for checks-agents.md, collection-reference.md, metrics-and-logs.md, api-quirks.md in the Router table and Appendix.

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The Router table ties each reference file to a specific triggering condition ('Operator says' / 'First read'), and other mentions specify exact use cases (e.g., consult api-quirks.md before interpreting responses).
tests.evidence: "AgentCore runtime will not start / cannot invoke | ListAgentRuntimes / GetAgentRuntime for status, version, role ARN | references/checks-agentcore.md (LLM-AC-001)"

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths of the form references/<filename>.md with no absolute paths or traversals.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile, consequential operations (permission checks, SCP correlation, alias resolution) are given exact API calls and ordering, while softer judgment areas (migration advisory framing, scope disclosure) are described with rationale rather than rigid scripts.
tests.evidence: "Simulate the runtime role with iam:SimulatePrincipalPolicy for every action it exercises... any required action denied is LLM-AC-001 (CRITICAL)." vs. advisory framing like "This is advisory, not an outage: a Classic agent that still works is not a reason to skip it."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: Where multiple options exist (e.g., migration paths), one is marked as the closer analog/default while the other is an alternative, and the skill doesn't present competing tools as equal unqualified menus.
tests.evidence: "recommend migrating via the AgentCore harness (config-based, closest analog) or code-defined agents on AgentCore" — harness positioned as the primary/closer analog.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The procedures teach a generalizable approach (resolve alias before concluding production behavior, check role permissions then SCPs, etc.) applicable to any runtime/agent instance, not a one-off declaration.
tests.evidence: "Resolve each alias with ListAgentAliases / GetAgentAlias to the version it serves; treat that version — not the latest prepared DRAFT — as production behaviour" — a reusable rule, not tied to one specific agent.

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has a dedicated 'Common wrong answers' section plus an 'Error Handling' section documenting specific traps (alias vs DRAFT, denied AgentCore reads, no-datapoints vs zero), satisfying the gotchas requirement.
tests.evidence: "'GetAgent shows PREPARED, so that config is what production runs.' An agent's live behaviour is its alias → version resolution, not the latest prepared DRAFT."

tests.name: Templates and outputs missing
tests.reasoning: The skill produces structured review reports and provides an explicit template asset referenced for that purpose.
tests.evidence: "assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md — consolidated review output (scope, findings with check-ids and severities, remediation, disclosed gaps)"

tests.name: Templates and outputs must not be in body
tests.reasoning: No large inline output template exists in the body; the report template is correctly offloaded to assets/ and only referenced.
tests.evidence: "the output follows assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md" — template content itself is not duplicated inline.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked
tests.reasoning: The single asset file is referenced in both the validation checklist and the appendix.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md."

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: The asset reference specifies the triggering condition (when a full report is requested) for loading the template.
tests.evidence: "When a full report is requested, the output follows assets/agent-runtime-report-template.md."

tests.name: Asset path format
tests.reasoning: The asset link uses a relative path from skill root with no traversal or absolute path.

tests.name: Step-by-step guidance
tests.reasoning: Both procedures (AgentCore review and Bedrock Agents Classic review) use the checkbox checklist format with 'Step N:' labeling as required, and no detailed sub-sections exist that diverge from this numbering.
tests.evidence: "- [ ] Step 1: Read the runtime with bedrock-agent:ListAgentRuntimes / GetAgentRuntime..." and "- [ ] Step 1: Enumerate agents with bedrock-agent:ListAgents..."

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit 'Before You Present — Validate Your Own Output' section instructing the agent to re-check findings, evidence, masking, and disclosed gaps before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before you present an agent/runtime review, re-check your own output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
